Subject: SOC 2 re-attestation and renewal prep - AuroraApps

Hi Naomi,

Hope you had a good week. Our renewal with Redwood comes up in Feb and Legal has asked for a fresh SOC 2 re-attestation for the current year as part of the renewal checklist. We also expect a product spike in Q2 that will push our concurrent seat needs from 20 -> ~35, and we need guidance on the evidence/retention side to make sure the re-attestation goes smoothly.

Key asks from our side:
- A list of the exact evidence artifacts Redwood will provide for the re-attestation (logs, change history, control mappings)
- How long you retain audit logs and options to extend retention to 24 months for our account
- A recommended sequencing for handing over evidence (we have a limited window in late Jan for transfers)
- Rough pricing for a temporary seat onramp (20 -> 35) and any short-term burst options we can use for evidence export

I've attached a spreadsheet (soc2_attestation_request.xlsx) with the items Legal flagged. Can you confirm who on your side will own the technical export and the commercial amendment?

Thanks — can we sync early next week for 30 minutes?

Tanya Singh
Head of Security Ops, AuroraApps

Thanks Tanya — great to hear from you and noted. High level: we can support the re-attestation and the capacity uplift, and we can scope the evidence handoff to fit your late-Jan window.

Proposed next steps (for our call):
1) Technical runbook: Ben will own the log/export manifest and S3 transfer instructions. He can outline the export cadence and the temporary burst capacity needed for the transfer.
2) Commercial: Marissa will propose an amendment for the seat increase + extended retention; we can offer a short-term burst for evidence transfer to avoid committing to long-term seats immediately.
3) Timeline: draft evidence list and access by Dec 28; bulk export window Jan 10-20; final bundle submitted to your auditors by Feb 1.

I attached a short renewal_playbook_draft.pdf with the sequencing I usually use. If AuroraApps wants longer-than-default retention (24 months) we include that as an add-on in the amendment (pricing below will reflect that).

Can you share any constraints on how Aurora wants to receive logs (S3 vs. secure SCP vs. partner transfer)? If S3, we prefer a write-only temp bucket approach.

I’ll set up a 30min slot for Tue.

– Naomi

Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation and renewal prep - evidence sequencing and exports

Thanks Naomi / Tanya — looping in technical details here.

Quick summary of what we can deliver and constraints:
- Deliverables: consolidated control-mapped evidence bundle (config snapshots, change logs, auth logs, deployment manifests), continuous audit log export for window, and a signed attestation summary (PDF).
- Default log retention: 12 months. We can add a 24-month retention policy as an account-level add-on.
- Export method: preferred = AWS S3 (temporary write-only role), fallback = encrypted SCP. We do not accept inbound unencrypted HTTP uploads.
- Throughput for bulk export: default rate = ~120 GB/day; temporary burst can be arranged up to 600 GB/day for a 72-hour window if planned in advance.

Action items for Aurora (what we need from you):
- A dedicated S3 bucket and an IAM role ARN with write-only permissions (we will provide a policy template).
- Exact retention mapping per log type (audit, app, auth, kv-cache) — see attached manifest.
- A point of contact for the transfer window (name + mobile).

Attached: log_export_manifest.json (schema of files we will include) and s3_transfer_instructions.txt (policy template + steps).

Proposed timeline (hard):
- Dec 28: Aurora provides S3 role + retention mapping
- Jan 12-14: bulk export window (reserve additional burst Jan 15-17 if needed)
- Jan 25: internal evidence validation and handoff to auditors

If you want us to push more aggressively (earlier delivery), we can compress but will need a larger burst window and a one-time handling fee.

– Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
attachments: log_export_manifest.json; s3_transfer_instructions.txt

Hi team — jumping in on the commercial side. Naomi, Ben: thank you for the clear sequencing. Tanya: here is how we can structure the amendment and pricing for the uplift.

Commercial outline (draft):
- Seat uplift: 20 -> 35, 12-month commitment for the uplift portion at 20% discount vs list. Option to decommit after 90 days with pro-rated usage charges.
- Retention add-on: 24-month audit-log retention as an account add-on priced monthly. One-time evidence handling fee (covers additional engineering burst and prep).
- Evidence burst credit: we can apply a $3,000 credit toward the one-time handling fee if you sign the amendment by Jan 5.

I attached an amendment_term_sheet.xlsx with line items and a DocuSign link — if that looks reasonable I can route for signature and we can apply the credit immediately. After signature, we will schedule the burst reserve and confirm the export window.

Proposed next dates: DocuSign route by Dec 28; sign by Jan 5 to secure the credit; bulk export Jan 12-17.
